limits: Command is strongest over demons, corrupted spaces, and sin-aligned subjects, and far less absolute against unrelated sovereigns or purified domains.
The throne line can be challenged by rival claimants, superior infernal ranks, broken contracts, or holy suppression.
Infernal authority weakens when the bearer rejects the obligations, bargains, and symbolic acts that legitimize the bloodline.

worldCompatibility: Demonic Heritage Throne governs infernal hierarchy within a bounded hell-linked order and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the deepest cosmic law.

Its power remains coherent because it is lineage-bound, contestable, vice-fed, and highly vulnerable to stronger spiritual opposition or broken legitimacy.

name: Damage Reflection Field
summary: A retributive Authority that turns incoming harm into lawful backlash within a bounded field of punishment.

Its progression bias favors endurance, timing, and punishment of overcommitment rather than pure mitigation or passive tanking. The bearer becomes strongest against enemies who rely on burst damage, arrogance, or mindless repetition of force. Convert judged incoming damage into reflected punishment, retrition charge, or empowered counter-effects based on how recklessly the enemy attacked.
Release stored retribution at the right moment before the field collapses under pressure, denial, or misread threat profiles.
progression: Early growth improves reflection efficiency, field clarity, and the bearer's ability to convert straightforward attacks into safe retaliation.
Mid progression unlocks rider effects such as stun, shred, burnback, or judgment marks on attackers who keep violating the field.
Late progression turns the bearer into a terrifying punitive fortress whose enemies can destroy themselves simply by refusing to respect its law.

In implementation, it maps well to reflected-damage rules, attack qualification tags, field uptime, and retribution-charge states. Those hooks fit existing combat logic without needing a separate subsystem for every retaliatory effect. They also create readable UI and narrator language around punishment windows. That makes the Authority easy to integrate cleanly.

The player should feel powerful when they correctly read enemy aggression and punished when they treat reflection like unconditional immunity. That preserves the authority fantasy while keeping encounter variety healthy. The strongest version feels like judgment under fire, not lazy invincibility.
limits: Only attacks that meaningfully enter the field's judged boundary can be reflected or converted into retribution value.

The field can collapse if the bearer takes too much unprocessed pressure or misjudges which forms of harm it can lawfully answer.
costs: Reflection requires taking real pressure, which can exhaust, wound, or destabilize the bearer even when the punishment is successful.
Holding the field at high intensity consumes energy and attention that would otherwise go to offense or mobility.
Overreliance on retribution can push the bearer toward a reactive mindset that lets enemies choose too much of the battle's tempo.
worldCompatibility: Damage Reflection Field governs a bounded law of retributive harm and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and stronger immunity or negation orders.
It is compatible with defensive combat, punish mechanics, escort scenarios, and dueling because it commands a narrow retaliatory domain.
Its power stays coherent because it depends on field jurisdiction, incoming force, and counterplay instead of universal damage denial.

name: Law Comprehension Codex
summary: A jurisprudential Authority that traces local laws, interprets their clauses, and imposes bounded rule edits within understood domains.
description: Law Comprehension Codex is an Authority that grants the bearer ruling-grade understanding of how specific laws in the world are structured and enforced. It belongs in the Authority category because it governs command through interpreted law, lawful override windows, and domain-limited rule precedence rather than through generic intelligence or reality editing. The bearer learns to trace a phenomenon, identify the governing clause behind it, and then exploit or temporarily amend that clause where they have earned standing. Its progression bias favors study, precision, and local dominion over a known rule set rather than reckless omnidirectional power. The Authority is strongest when the bearer has properly read a site, artifact, ritual, or enemy technique before trying to intervene. The main tradeoff is interpretive burden, because misunderstanding the active law can lead to failed commands, catastrophic backlash, or accidental empowerment of the very rule being challenged. In the world, Law Comprehension Codex should terrify scholars, judges, mages, and primordial guardians because it turns knowledge into a form of jurisdiction. coreLoop: Trace a natural, magical, or social phenomenon until the Codex identifies the governing law fragment behind it.
Accumulate lawful standing and fragments so the bearer can issue a bounded amendment, suspension, or counter-clause inside that domain.
Exploit the edited law before correction pressure, hostile guardians, or missing context collapse the advantage.
progression: Early growth improves law tracing, fragment storage, and safe intervention in narrow local rules such as motion, heat, or ritual sequencing.
Mid progression unlocks codified domains, chained clause edits, and stronger standing against magical, contractual, or battlefield laws.
Late progression turns the bearer into a feared juris-architect who can make even mighty powers obey the letter of a law they failed to read closely enough.
narrativeHooks: Reality does not merely warp around you; it starts revealing which clauses people have trusted without ever understanding.

The deeper your understanding grows, the harder it becomes to pretend the world was ever held together by simple rules.
questHooks: Repair a corrupted region by identifying which foundational law was broken and who benefits from keeping it unstable.
Win a battle against a stronger foe by forcing their signature technique to obey an older clause it normally ignores.
Steal a sealed page of the Codex from a guardian court that insists mortals must never learn how law is actually written.
possibleUses: In gameplay, Law Comprehension Codex can support trace-and-edit mechanics, domain-specific counters, lawful immunities, and localized rule manipulation. It gives high-intellect play a command fantasy instead of only passive analysis. That makes solving encounters feel procedural and sovereign at the same time. It also works across combat, puzzles, rituals, and environmental hazards.

In narrative and quests, it enables tribunal drama, broken-zone restoration, ancient-rule archaeology, and morally dangerous questions about who gets to revise what everyone else calls natural law. The bearer can save people by restoring the proper rule or become feared for proving that stability was always negotiable. That creates strong philosophical tension. It also gives the narrator a precise language for wonder and dread.

In implementation, it maps well to tagged law domains, traceable phenomena, local amendment windows, and correction backlash. Those hooks can enrich ritual systems, encounter scripting, dungeon hazards, and prompt context without requiring unrestricted reality editing everywhere. They also let designers decide exactly which content is law-readable. That makes the Authority powerful but tractable to ship.

Its limitation-aware use comes from requiring comprehension before command. The player should feel brilliant when they read a system correctly and punished when they guess wrong. That preserves the dignity of law as something interpreted and contested rather than casually rewritten on impulse. The strongest version feels like jurisdiction earned through study, not free reality authorship.
limits: Only traced and sufficiently understood laws can be challenged, amended, or suspended by the Codex.
Complex conceptual laws require fragments, standing, and preparation that cannot be improvised in every scene.
Guarded domains, sovereign authorities, and misunderstood clauses can all reject the bearer's command outright.
costs: Tracing and editing law consumes immense focus, energy, and interpretive risk, especially against layered or ancient rules.
Every intervention attracts correction pressure, scrutiny from guardians, and the possibility of rule backlash if the edit is unstable.
The bearer risks becoming emotionally detached as more of the world starts to look like clauses to be parsed instead of lives to be lived.
worldCompatibility: Law Comprehension Codex governs bounded domains of interpreted law and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the deepest cosmic structure.
It is compatible with ritual systems, contracts, hazard logic, and domain contests because it commands readable rules rather than unrestricted existence.
Its power remains coherent because it depends on tracing, standing, and local jurisdiction instead of universal permission to edit reality.

name: Divine Champion (God's Chosen)
summary: A consecrated Authority that appoints the bearer as a god-backed champion with domain-limited miracles, command, and holy legitimacy.
description: Divine Champion is an Authority that marks the bearer as a chosen combat and judgment instrument of a deity or pantheon. It belongs in the Authority category because it grants command through sanctioned holy office, domain-backed miracles, and the right to act in a god's name within bounded sacred scope. The bearer does not simply receive blessings, but becomes a recognized champion whose title carries real metaphysical weight with allies, enemies, relics, and rites. Its progression bias favors devotion, trial completion, public legitimacy, and faithful action rather than private self-optimization. The Authority grows strongest when the champion acts within the moral, ritual, or jurisdictional lane of their patron's sphere. The main tradeoff is burden, because divine office comes with vows, scrutiny, and the constant risk of misrepresenting a higher will. In the world, Divine Champion should command reverence, envy, and political alarm because a god-backed mortal can overturn earthly balances without being a god themselves. coreLoop: Act under the champion's seal to invoke miracles, rally allies, and enforce the patron's sacred right within situations the office recognizes.
Complete divine trials, uphold vows, and resolve patron-aligned crises to deepen legitimacy and widen the office's lawful reach.
Manage public worship, rival clergy, and the cost of being the mortal face of a power far larger than yourself.
progression: Early growth grants the champion's seal, minor miracles, and recognized authority in the patron's first sphere such as war, judgment, healing, or flame.
Mid progression expands into relic command, group blessing fields, and stronger miracle law when the champion acts under rite or sanction.
Late progression turns the bearer into a world-shaping sacred officer whose arrival can sanctify battlefields, rally nations, or condemn blasphemous powers.

Your victories are never fully private because every miracle becomes evidence for or against the patron you represent.
The more clearly you hear divine purpose, the harder it becomes to separate your own desires from the office speaking through you.
questHooks: Prove your office in a public trial where rival faiths are waiting for one failed miracle to discredit the god behind you.
Recover a relic that will either strengthen your patron's authority in the world or expose why your appointment was contested from the start.
Choose whether to obey a divine command that would save a kingdom at the cost of betraying someone innocent.
possibleUses: In gameplay, Divine Champion can support miracle skills, sanctified zones, relic permissions, ally-rally effects, and patron-domain command actions. It also gives designers a clean way to gate sacred interactions by legitimacy.

In narrative and quests, it enables faith politics, public trials, sacred warfare, and the tension of being used as proof that a god still intervenes. The bearer can inspire whole regions or destabilize them just by appearing under the right seal. They can also be crushed by expectations no ordinary mortal was built to carry. That gives the Authority strong emotional and institutional weight.

In implementation, it maps well to patron domains, vow states, sanction flags, miracle permissions, and relic recognition. Those hooks can feed faction systems, combat buffs, story checks, and narrator voice without requiring a full theology sim. They also create space for revocation, doubt, and contested legitimacy. That makes the Authority highly expressive while still manageable.

Its limitation-aware use comes from keeping power tied to office and patron scope. The player should feel incredible when acting as a true champion and meaningfully constrained when their god's domain or vows do not justify intervention. That preserves divine gravitas without reducing the setting to constant holy override. The strongest version feels like sanctioned command, not blank-check sainthood.
limits: Champion power is bounded by patron domain, vow integrity, and whether the current situation falls within the office's recognized sacred scope.
Miracles weaken when the bearer acts in bad faith, breaks sanction, or tries to force authority into matters their patron does not lawfully govern.
Relics, temples, and allied faithful may reject or question a champion whose legitimacy has become disputed.
costs: Divine office imposes vows, ritual obligations, and constant moral scrutiny from both worshippers and enemies.
Public miracle use escalates political tension because every visible intervention changes who seems favored by the heavens.
Failure, doubt, or misrepresentation can trigger revocation, crisis of faith, or devastating backlash from disappointed believers.
worldCompatibility: Divine Champion governs patron-backed sacred office and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the highest order that even gods must answer to.
It is compatible with faith politics, relic systems, miracle combat, and public-legitimacy arcs because it commands a bounded holy domain.
Its power stays coherent because it depends on office, vows, sanction, and patron scope rather than unrestricted holy superiority.

name: Heaven's Mandate (Fate's Favorite)

Spend that legitimacy to survive crises, sway succession struggles, or make key opportunities align in your favor when your claim is under pressure.
Preserve the Mandate by acting in ways that keep heaven's endorsement believable to the world and to the deeper order behind it.

Rebels, prophets, and rival heirs all gain reasons to expose your failures as evidence that the Mandate was never truly yours.
The more destiny bends toward you, the more dangerous it becomes to confuse endorsement with virtue.
questHooks: Hold a collapsing realm together long enough to prove heaven has not withdrawn its favor from your rule.
Confront a rival claimant whose omens are stronger than yours but whose heart may be far less fit to rule.
Recover a lost regalia that can either confirm your legitimacy or expose that the Mandate has been contested all along.

limits: The Mandate is strongest in contexts where legitimacy, succession, and public recognition matter, and far less absolute in purely private or chaotic conflict.

worldCompatibility: Heaven's Mandate governs legitimacy, karmic favor, and worldly succession while remaining beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the highest cosmic order.
It is compatible with rulership arcs, dynastic conflict, omen systems, and fate-weighted progression because it commands a bounded regime of heavenly endorsement.
Its power stays coherent because it depends on recognition, conduct, and public crisis rather than unrestricted plot immunity.

name: Celestial Pact (Divine Contract System)

The Authority is strongest when the bearer honors contract terms, fulfills patron errands, and acts within the pact's recognized sphere. progression: Early growth grants a dangerous but usable pact mark, first-tier authority effects, and a clear debt structure the bearer must survive.
Mid progression expands into stronger patron manifestations, enforcement clauses, and partial command over beings or spaces touched by the same blood law.
Late progression turns the bearer into a feared contract sovereign whose words can bind, punish, or unleash horrors at the cost of becoming harder to call wholly mortal.
narrativeHooks: Every pact mark on your body is a sentence in a contract others can learn to fear, read, or exploit.
People near you must guess whether they are dealing with a desperate mortal using dark office or a person already halfway replaced by the patron's claim.
The more elegant your command becomes, the more frightening it is that power now speaks in a language written with your own blood.
questHooks: Break or rewrite one clause of the pact before your patron cashes it in during the worst possible crisis.
Hunt a rival warlock whose contract exposes a weakness in your own authority's legal foundation.
Choose whether to buy enough power to save a city tonight even though tomorrow's debt may ruin everything you value.
possibleUses: In gameplay, Blood Pact Warlock can support debt-backed power surges, pact clauses, patron manifestations, and dark-command actions unavailable to ordinary casters. It gives warlock fantasy a true authority structure instead of only dangerous spellcasting. That makes every activation feel contractual and loaded. It also creates strong synergy with corruption, summons, and taboo systems.

In narrative and quests, it enables bargain horror, patron politics, cursed rescues, and choices where the clean option simply does not exist anymore. The bearer can save lives by paying with their own future or doom others by pretending the debt is manageable. That creates excellent moral pressure. It also keeps dark power intimate and personal instead of abstractly evil.

In implementation, it maps well to contract states, debt counters, patron domains, clause unlocks, and backlash events. Those hooks can enrich combat, quests, and narrator framing without requiring a unique subsystem for every dark patron. They also create readable escalation paths for corruption and repayment. That makes the Authority strong and implementable.

Its limitation-aware use comes from making every gain owed. The player should feel brilliant and frightened whenever the pact solves a problem too cleanly. That preserves the dark-contract fantasy while keeping the patron meaningfully above the bearer. The strongest version feels like commanding borrowed doom under a signature written in blood.
limits: The pact only authorizes the powers and commands explicitly supported by the current contract and patron domain.
Broken payment schedules, rival legal claims, or damaged blood seals can sharply weaken or invalidate the authority.
Holy suppression, anti-contract rites, and patrons with stronger claim can interfere with the warlock's right to command.
costs: Every significant use deepens debt, corruption, or service obligation owed to the patron.
Escalating the pact may demand blood, memory, lifespan, loyalty, or acts the bearer cannot later undo.
The visible signs of dark authority create fear, isolation, and constant risk that others will try to exploit or purge the contract.
worldCompatibility: Blood Pact Warlock governs dark contractual authority and remains beneath Void, Grandmother Void, and the highest cosmic law.
It is compatible with patron systems, corruption arcs, summon control, and taboo magic because it commands a bounded blood-sealed office.
Its power stays coherent because it depends on clauses, debt, patron scope, and contestable legitimacy rather than free evil omnipotence.
